chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Ibn Muskān, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr and Faḍālah, from Ḥusayn, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, who said:
He narrated to me that he asked him about the two rakʿahs at the time of zawāl on Friday. He said: So he said: As for me, when the sun declines, I begin with the obligatory prayer.

key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ: the two units of prayer being asked about
key_terms.الزَّوَالِ: the sun’s decline from the meridian, marking the onset of noon prayer time
key_terms.بَدَأْتُ: I begin; indicating the order of performing the prayer
key_terms.بِالْفَرِيضَةِ: with the obligatory prayer, showing its precedence here
key_terms.زَالَتِ الشَّمْسُ: when the sun declines, indicating the relevant prayer time
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ: Friday, the day on which the ruling in question applies

ai.seo_question: On Friday at zawāl, should one begin with the two rakʿahs or with the obligatory prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling concerning two rakʿahs performed at the time of zawāl on Friday. The Imam عليه السلام states that when the sun declines, he begins with the obligatory prayer, indicating precedence of the farīḍah at that time.
